The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.clari.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", error="invalid_token"`. The protected-resource document reports resource `https://mcp.clari.com/mcp`, authorization server `https://mcp.clari.com/mcp`, bearer header support, and scopes `openid`, `profile`. The separate authorization-server metadata reports issuer `https://login.clari.com/oauth2/aus13shznanP7WOkp698`, authorization endpoint `https://app.clari.com/authorize`, token endpoint `https://login.clari.com/oauth2/aus13shznanP7WOkp698/v1/token`, registration endpoint `https://mcp.clari.com/okta/clients`, PKCE S256, DPoP algorithms RS256/384/512 and ES256/384/512, and token endpoint auth methods client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, client_secret_jwt, private_key_jwt. Its grant types are authorization_code, implicit, refresh_token, password, client_credentials, and urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code. It lists scopes openid, profile, email, address, phone, offline_access, device_sso. Revocation is at `https://login.clari.com/oauth2/aus13shznanP7WOkp698/v1/revoke`; token lifetime is not published in the supplied metadata.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The Forecast help article describes the MCP as a way to query live forecast data and says users need not open a forecast grid. It documents one forecast tab per query, so cross-tab rollups require multiple queries composed by the AI assistant. The public sources do not establish which additional UI operations humans can perform but the input `/mcp` endpoint cannot.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The Forecast setup article suggests asking Claude: “Am I connected to Clari MCP?” and “What forecast tabs do I have access to in Clari? Use the Clari MCP to answer this question.” It says these prompts test the connection. These are client/user suggestions; no evidence shows the server enforces them. The article instructs admins to enable the MCP and users to have an opted-in forecast tab.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The Forecast setup article states: “Permissions are scoped automatically: Users can only query forecast data within their existing Clari permissions and hierarchy — enabling MCP does not expand or change what data individual users can access.” It also states: “The MCP returns data scoped to one forecast tab per call.” The security addendum describes encryption at rest using AES 256-bit or higher, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit, and customer-account activity logs available through API. The privacy policy says it does not cover Customer Data processed on a customer's behalf; that data is governed by customer agreements.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor describes its MCP expansion as a “governed connection” and says write-back capabilities will allow AI tools to take action inside Salesloft and Clari. The July 2026 announcement describes several ecosystem integrations as rolling out through late summer 2026.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Forecast permissions and one-tab-per-query behavior are documented by Clari, but public schemas or code were unavailable to independently verify server enforcement. The security addendum's general logging and encryption statements are vendor commitments, not MCP-specific implementation details. The announced write-back capability is not tied to a public tool list or documented confirmation mechanism.

contradictions: The protected-resource metadata lists `https://mcp.clari.com/mcp` as an authorization server, while the path-specific authorization-server metadata identifies `https://login.clari.com/oauth2/aus13shznanP7WOkp698` as issuer and provides its OAuth endpoints.
The path-specific authorization-server metadata advertises `client_credentials` among grant types, while the supplied OpenID configuration's grant_types_supported omits it.

Clari's support article documents `https://mcp.clari.com/sse` for its Forecast MCP, whereas the input endpoint is `https://mcp.clari.com/mcp`. Public sources do not say whether these paths expose the same tools.

The support article describes Forecast MCP access and a one-forecast-tab-per-call boundary; the later newsroom announcement describes a broader Clari + Salesloft MCP expansion including execution data, conversations, forecasting, deal inspection, and write-back. Public tool names and endpoint-specific scope are unavailable.
observations_for_research: OAuth metadata is publicly discoverable even though the tool list is gated behind authentication; the resource scope list is narrower than the authorization server's advertised scope list.
Clari's documented Forecast MCP has an organization-admin enablement step and relies on the user's existing product permissions and forecast-tab opt-ins.

The vendor's newsroom announcement frames MCP as a shared revenue context layer across external AI systems and describes planned write-back; endpoint-specific tools and safeguards are not publicly enumerated.
